read_scope: Read the actual current complete three consumers and five suppliers, including their statements/definitions, Facts and local proofs. Reviewed exact uses, coefficient choices, quotient/sign conventions, AC, compactness/smoothness, finite-free homology and nilpotence hypotheses. External full texts and transitive supplier proofs were not newly audited. No prior Root report or native readiness result is attributed as this review.

reviews.consumer_locator: Definition, paragraphs 1–2 (Borel quotient, character classes, S and fractions)
reviews.match: Both assume AC and T=(R/Z)^r, use the same product right Milnor model, and identify (e.t,x)~(e,t.x) with the right diagonal action (e,x).t=(e.t,t^-1.x). Taking k=R, both use u_chi=c1 of the associated character line with the same inverse-character equivalence, S generated by all nontrivial character classes, and the identical torsion-aware fraction relation. The supplier proves character classes nonzero and closure with zero excluded; its fraction operations are exactly those adopted by the consumer, including r=0 giving S={1}.

reviews.consumer_locator: Definition, paragraphs 1–2 (coefficient ring and generator normalization)
reviews.match: The consumer explicitly assumes AC and the supplier’s standard product torus, period-one basis and product Milnor model. The supplier identifies H*(BT;R)=R[u1,...,ur] and Sym(t*) by e_i*->u_i of degree two, with u_i the real coefficient image of the complex-oriented tautological Euler generator. The consumer adopts precisely those generators rather than opposite-signed hyperplane classes. The r=0 coefficient ring R also agrees. No identification with Cartan, Chow or quotient-stack cohomology is inferred.

reviews.consumer_locator: Statement, localized extension; Facts F6; Proof 6.1 and 7.1
reviews.match: Both work under AC with the same right product Milnor model and k in {Q,R}. F6 uses the supplier’s fraction construction over H*(BT;k). By consumer 7.1 the constructed integration is coefficient-module-linear, so applying it to a witnessed equality t(s′alpha-s alpha′)=0 yields t(s′int(alpha)-s int(alpha′))=0; hence alpha/s->int(alpha)/s is well defined. The supplier supplies precisely S and this equivalence relation, not a localization theorem or ABBV formula. No smooth form model on the infinite base is required.

Consumer 1.1 establishes each fixed component F_j as compact smooth embedded and boundaryless; Hausdorffness, finite dimension and second countability are inherited from the ambient smooth-manifold convention, and the averaged Riemannian metric restricts to it. With AC and the same ordinary-product BT model, the supplier gives BT x F_j paracompact Hausdorff and of CW type. The consumer uses that conclusion for its Borel normal-bundle base. Numerability is obtained separately from the Milnor supplier and finite normal charts, so the base lemma is not misused as a Thom or orientation theorem. Ambient M need not be oriented.

Apply the supplier with k=R to compact smooth F_j and the restriction of the invariant Riemannian metric constructed in consumer 1.1; AC is present in both. It supplies N>=1 with the positive-degree ideal J satisfying J^N=0. After the consumer’s Kunneth identification, the ideal R_tensor_J also has Nth power zero, so n_j^N=0; localization preserves this equation. Thus consumer 5.1’s finite geometric series is valid. Empty fixed loci are treated vacuously, and normal rank zero retains Euler class 1; no oriented-manifold hypothesis is added.

Although its title emphasizes rational coefficients, the supplier expressly proves in 3.1 that H_q(BT;k) is finite dimensional in every degree for each k in {Q,R}. Consumer F3 uses exactly the real instance, under the same AC and product Milnor torus hypotheses, to discharge the finite-free factor hypothesis of the separately cited field Kunneth ring theorem. This yields H_T*(F_j;R)=H*(F_j;R) tensor R. Character classes are compatible with the tautological convention in supplier 3.2; no unsupported identification of rational and real cohomology rings is used.
